overview: This single-page file consists of a list-of-papers sheet for records concerning military activities in Japanese-ruled Taiwan (Formosa). It indexes one communication, dated March 2, 1934, apparently sent from Taipei to the U.S. Embassy in Japan, reporting the formation of societies intended to educate the public about spies and the compulsory training of adult Taiwanese Chinese. The sheet also directs readers to related decimal files 394.20 and 794.94.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: Military Activities in Formosa
subfiles.about: An index sheet records a March 2, 1934 communication about anti-spy educational societies and compulsory training for adult Taiwanese Chinese.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists one paper under the subject of military activities in Formosa. The indexed communication was dated March 2, 1934, and apparently originated in Taipei for the U.S. Embassy in Japan. Its subject was the formation of societies intended to educate people about the presence of spies and a report concerning compulsory training for adult Taiwanese Chinese; related material was noted under decimal classifications 394.20 and 794.94.

interest: The sheet is useful as evidence of how the State Department classified and cross-referenced intelligence about militarization and civil mobilization in colonial Taiwan. Although the underlying communication is absent, its précis points to organized anti-espionage propaganda and compulsory adult training as early as 1934. The cross-references may help historians locate related records elsewhere in the Department’s decimal file.
